title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 3: a letter written with the Spirit, the service of the Spirit and of death, and the veil that is taken away.

questions.text: What does the writer call the Corinthians themselves in verse 2?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says: You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men.

answers.text: Our crown and our glory
Our letter, written in our hearts
Our tablets of stone
Our temple in Corinth

questions.text: With what, and on what, is this letter of Christ written, according to verse 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says it is written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God, not in tablets of stone, but in tablets that are hearts of flesh.

answers.text: With ink, on tablets of stone, as at the first
With the hand of Moses, on a scroll of a book
With tears, in a book sealed until the end
With the Spirit of the living God, in tablets that are hearts of flesh

questions.text: Where does their sufficiency come from, according to verse 5?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says they are not sufficient of themselves to account anything as from themselves, but their sufficiency is from God.

answers.text: From God
From themselves
From the letters of commendation
From the children of Israel

questions.text: What does verse 6 say about the letter and the Spirit?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says they were made sufficient as servants of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit, for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

answers.text: Both the letter and the Spirit give life
The letter gives life, but the Spirit kills
The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life
Neither the letter nor the Spirit remains

questions.text: What could the children of Israel not do, because of the glory of Moses' face?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face, which was passing away.

answers.text: They could not speak to him
They could not look steadfastly on his face
They could not carry the tablets
They could not hear his voice

questions.text: How does verse 9 compare the service of condemnation and the service of righteousness?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says that if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.

answers.text: The service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory
Both of them have exactly the same glory
The service of condemnation has the greater glory
Neither of them has any glory at all

questions.text: What did Moses put on his face, according to verse 13?
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says Moses put a veil on his face, so that the children of Israel would not look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.

answers.text: Oil
Ashes
A crown
A veil

questions.text: When is the veil taken away, according to verse 16?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says that whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

answers.text: When the old covenant is read aloud
When Moses is honored
Whenever someone turns to the Lord
When the letter is obeyed

questions.text: What does verse 17 say is found where the Spirit of the Lord is?
questions.explanation: Verse 17 says that the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

answers.text: Liberty
Silence
Condemnation
A veil

questions.text: What happens to those who see the glory of the Lord with unveiled face?
questions.explanation: Verse 18 says they are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.

answers.text: They are hardened in their minds and hearts
They are transformed into the same image from glory to glory
They are covered with a veil once again
They become servants of the letter that kills
